synopsis: Hexagon supplies the Vehicle Intervention System for surface-mining haulage rather than acting as a machine OEM; its functions include propulsion inhibition, retarder and service braking, following-distance control and overspeed intervention [f1661, f1663]. On 25 March 2026, Hexagon announced that its current-generation system had passed the University of Pretoria’s TRL4 verification before integrated site testing, describing it as the first open-pit Level 9 system to pass that gate [f1350, f1351]. The case validated detection, tracking, warnings, diagnostics and intervention, with evidence acceptance involving an independent university gate and customers [f1843, f1848]. Its 2024 product evolution added 4D radar, with people and vehicles listed as targets; an earlier generation accumulated more than 10,000 working-mine test hours, which should not be attributed to the current generation [f1664, f1353]. Build time, TRL4 test duration, speed and direction, speed range, weather envelope and object-size specifications were not found, and the March 2026 press release provided no numbers, limiting its usefulness for quantitative timing and operating-envelope planning [f1359, f1666, f6373].
